_comment: Human decisions where the sources genuinely disagree.
The build FAILS on any conflict not listed here, so this file is the
project's record of why the data says what it says — the thing the
original build never had. Every entry needs a written reason.
Entries are APPLIED, not merely recorded: 'chose: rulebook' writes the
book's value into the dataset with provenance, and 'chose: battlescribe'
keeps the catalogue's. Either way the build checks the stated value
against the source it names and fails if the two have drifted apart.
A layer superseding the rulebook is NOT a conflict and does not belong
here: the pipeline resolves that by precedence (Dispatch > rulebook >
catalogue). Only add an entry when two sources of the same standing
state different things, or when one is more precise than the model can
The same keys also rule on a REPRINT disagreement: where a supplement
reprints an entry the dataset already carries and the two printings differ,
the build reports it here rather than picking a side. One entry answers
both checks, and each validates it from its own end — the reprint check
against the supplement, applyResolutions against the dataset and the book.

Combat Biologist.cost.ducats.because: Carcass Front reprints the Combat Biologist and prints the Ducat glyph on 'Cost: 3' where Warbands of Trench Crusade prints the Glory glyph on the same number. The number agrees; only the currency glyph differs. Glory is right: it is what the Warbands book prints, what Mercenaries.cat prices the model at, and what every other Mercenary in the game costs (2 to 7 Glory, none in Ducats). A Mercenary for 3 Ducats would be the cheapest model in Trench Crusade by a factor of six. Treated as a misprint or a font substitution in the Carcass Front PDF; reported every build so it cannot go quiet.

Combat Biologist.cost.glory.because: The other half of the same disagreement — see Combat Biologist.cost.ducats. Warbands of Trench Crusade and Mercenaries.cat both price the Combat Biologist at 3 Glory; the Carcass Front reprint of the entry sets the Ducat glyph on the same number. Every other field of the reprint agrees with what ships (Movement, Ranged, Melee, Armour, Base), which is what makes the currency glyph a glyph problem rather than a rules change.

Scripture Guardian.stats.ranged.because: The book gives the Scripture Guardian no Ranged characteristic ('-'); the catalogue lists '+1 Dice'. The book is authoritative over the community catalogue, and the entry's own text supports it — the Guardian attacks with Vengeful Scripture, a Special-type weapon with its own profile, rather than a normal Ranged characteristic. Flagged for upstream correction. Applies to the unlayered base ruleset only: Trench Dispatch 01 sets this field to +2 DICE and supersedes both sources in the layered ruleset.

Mamluk Faris.stats.armour.because: The Warbands book prints '-2 (-3)' — the parenthesised value is a conditional the entity model cannot yet express (it applies only in specific circumstances). The catalogue's flat -2 is the base value and is correct for roster building. Revisit when Statline gains conditional modifiers; tracked as a Phase 2 item.

Combat Medic.cost.ducats.because: The book prints 'Cost: 65' for the New Antioch Combat Medic; New Antioch.cat prices the same model at 40. The gap is exactly the Battlekit the book says a Medic always has: Standard Armour 15 + Gas Mask 5 + Medi-kit 5 = 25, and 40 + 25 = 65. The catalogue forces those three onto the model (min=1 entryLinks) and hides the matching Armoury rows from it, but leaves all three entryLinks unpriced, so its roster total comes to 40 — the split cost was never charged. The book is authoritative over the community catalogue and its figure is the one a player computes at the table. CAVEAT: nothing yet stops a Medic buying a second Gas Mask or Medi-kit from the New Antioch Armoury, which would double-charge by 10; the catalogue expresses that as a conditional 'hidden' modifier the pipeline does not read. Tracked with the forced-Battlekit gap below.
